intervals.label: discovery run
intervals.note: The first large asymmetry came in "a long weekend of work" just after New Year 1957 (month precision). The paper also reports follow-up measurements; their dates are not given, so the end is the publication-date bound of the completed interval.
intervals.quote: convert a Friday Chinese-lunch discussion, just after New Year, 1957, into a Tuesday morning major experimental observation.

quantity.quote: We plotted the trajectories of pions produced by 400-MeV protons hitting a target inside the machine

name: Nevis parity-violation experiment in pion and muon decay
notes: Included although outside the nine core targets: sourced by the APS landing page and Lederman's Nobel lecture, at a fixed laboratory. The Nevis cyclotron is not an Atlas accelerator record (not assigned to this stream), so accelerator_ids is empty.
No collaboration record: a three-author Columbia group (Garwin, Lederman, Weinrich). The Wu experiment at the National Bureau of Standards is not recorded (see the stream log).

Lederman did not receive a Nobel Prize for this experiment (his 1988 prize was for the neutrino beam method); Lederman's lecture says it "established the two-component neutrinos" and, with later decay-parameter work, "the V-A structure of the weak interactions".

physics_goals.quote: The “effect” here was the asymmetry in the emission of electrons around the incident, stopped, and spinning polarized muon.
physics_goals.value: Look for an asymmetry in the emission of decay electrons around the spin of a stopped, polarized muon, as a test of parity violation in the pion-muon-electron chain

summary.plain: In January 1957, after Chien-Shiung Wu reported at Christmas 1956 that cobalt-60 decay violated parity, Richard Garwin, Leon Lederman and Marcel Weinrich used Columbia's Nevis cyclotron to make polarized muons and saw a large asymmetry in where the decay electrons went: a clear break of mirror symmetry.
summary.technical: Stopped, polarized mu+ from pion decay in flight at the Nevis synchrocyclotron (about 400 MeV protons); decay-electron asymmetry of about 50 standard deviations with the muon spin precessing in a field; also gave g(μ⁺) = +2.00 ± 0.10 and showed that charge conjugation is violated.

unique_capabilities.quote: a correlation of the muon spin relative to its CM momentum would, in fact, be preserved in the kinematics of pion decay-in-flight, resulting in a polarized muon beam
unique_capabilities.value: A polarized muon beam from pion decay in flight at a cyclotron
